requirements.rule: SUB-SECTOR RULES (chimica and ceramica, art. 67-68, stesura 16 July 2024 pp. 89-95): their five biennial increments (seniority_increments_by_subsector) and three apprenticeship groups each (tracks naming the sub-sector) are modelled; apprentices 6 EUR per increment from 2025. Not modelled: the track of the impiegati amministrativi of all sectors (3 years, 70-90%), the fixed allowances of the sub-sector levels (such as the indennità di funzione of 6S), and their category, left to Employment.category.
requirements.remediation: Model the impiegati amministrativi track by category and the allowances of the sub-sector levels.

requirements.rule: SUB-SECTORS (verbale integrativo of 22 July 2024, pp. 5-6): the chimica, concia, gomma, plastica and vetro table is modelled as the sub-sector chimica (the base_salary_by_subsector chimica of levels 1-6 and the chimica levels 5s and 7), the ceramica, terracotta, gres and decorazione di piastrelle table as the sub-sector ceramica (levels A-G), both by EmployerProfile.subsector. Not modelled: the calzaturiero, lavorazioni a mano e su misura, pulitintolavanderie and occhialeria tables of the same verbale. Level 6S requested with chimica, and levels 1-6S with ceramica, are paid the tessile table, which those sectors do not print; levels 1-6 of chimica take the tessile seniority amounts and apprenticeship tracks.
requirements.remediation: Model the other sector tables, source the seniority and apprenticeship of chimica and ceramica and reject the levels their tables lack, then remove this note.

requirements.rule: INPS RATES: the employer and worker INPS rates of the sector (artigianato) are totals no 2026 INPS or association table confirms: the only component split found is the INPS guide of 2012 and the 2026 totals come from a software house page that does not prove its year. The contributions of every run rest on them.
requirements.remediation: Source the artigianato rates of 2026 on an INPS or association table, mark the inps block of contribution/2026/artigianato.json derived, then remove this note.

requirements.rule: LEVEL CATEGORY: all levels left null (no primary-source text confirming operaio/impiegato split). The 2026-artigianato.json tier applies the impiegato rate (0.2471) for category='impiegato'/'quadro' vs. default 0.2693. Employer cost for higher levels (5, 6, 6S) may be slightly overestimated until categories are confirmed from primary CCNL text.
requirements.remediation: Confirm the operaio/impiegato category of each level from the CCNL text.
Verify the value on its primary source and record the provenance; a derivation states its formula and inputs.

requirements.rule: The CCNL tier and the comporto are counted on the days of one episode and the relapses it continues. A CCNL that sums the sickness of separate episodes over a window (a calendar year, the last three years) can reach a lower tier or the end of the comporto earlier than the engine shows. The run is affected when an earlier episode outside the relapse chain is recorded. A CCNL whose comporto the engine counts over the calendar year (Commercio Art. 186 and the others with comporto_calendar_year) is not affected.
requirements.calculation: ccnl_engine.sickness.day.rules (CCNL tier of a sick day)
requirements.remediation: Add the cumulation window of each CCNL to its sickness rule, with the source, and count the tier and the comporto over it.

requirements.rule: L. 260/1949 art. 5 pays the workers with a fixed salary a further daily quota only for the civil holidays (25 April, 1 May, 2 June) falling on a Sunday; the other holidays of art. 2 (1 January, 6 January, Easter Monday, 15 August, 4 October, 1 November, 8 December, 25 and 26 December) give it only by CCNL clause, and the payment of 4 November is a CCNL institute. A run of a month with such a holiday on a Sunday, in a CCNL whose clause is not sourced (work_rules.sunday_holidays), pays the statutory holidays only; a public employment is paid none, its treatment not being sourced.
requirements.calculation: ccnl_engine.compensation.sunday_holiday.services.sunday_holiday; L. 260/1949 artt. 2 and 5 (Normattiva, art. 2 page sha256 42631c3dd629fe3a1c5e10efc7e3b7b86bb5a2b5325024aa4105eaadfcb49828, art. 5 page sha256 dbd670c663744af9); L. 54/1977 art. 1 (page sha256 cde3b9773f4411d28334a85bebdf9358fc4c161d745772df70f38bc79f48d09e)
requirements.remediation: Source the CCNL clause on the holidays falling on a Sunday and record it as work_rules.sunday_holidays.
